news.title: El Centro and KU partner on data-driven statewide effort to build a fuller picture of Latino communities in Kansas
news.summary_en: El Centro, a Latino-led, Latino-serving nonprofit organization based in Kansas City, Kansas, is leading an initiative to create a comprehensive, community-led portrait of the Latino experience in Kansas with the KU Center for Community Health and Development.

news.title: KU School of Music to present annual Vespers concerts on Dec. 6
news.summary_en: The University of Kansas School of Music will present its annual Vespers concerts Dec. 6, with performances at 2:30 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. at the Lied Center of Kansas. Tickets are now available.

news.title: KU evolutionary genetics researcher wins Big 12 Faculty of the Year Award
news.summary_en: John Kelly, professor of ecology & evolutionary biology, has been recognized as KU’s Big 12 Faculty of the Year recipient. His research helps explain why genetic diversity persists and demonstrates evolution in real time.

news.title: Art exhibition at KU Medical Center highlights healthy aging, partnership with Spencer Museum
news.summary_en: An art exhibition opening at the University of Kansas Medical Center this week uses visual, sound and interactive elements to explore age-friendly healthcare. The show is the result of a partnership with the Spencer Museum of Art to embed Kansas artists within the Kansas 4M Interprofessional Age Friendly Scholars program.

news.title: New documentary chronicles link between racial trauma, mental health experienced by Asian American communities
news.summary_en: In a new documentary, a professor of sociology at the University of Kansas weaves together personal testimony, historical analysis and creative artistic expression to illuminate the layered realities of racial trauma in AAPI (Asian American Pacific Islander) communities.

news.title: The Commons announces Red Hot Research dates for fall 2026
news.summary_en: The Commons will host Red Hot Research events for University of Kansas faculty on Oct. 30, Nov. 6 and Dec. 4. One Red Hot Graduate Research event will take place Nov. 13.
